request: Bech32 decoding must reject every malformed input with a descriptive error and must never panic, for any input bytes: non-ASCII characters anywhere in the string and data parts too short to hold a checksum included. Valid strings must round-trip through Encode and Decode unchanged.

defects.description: Decode lowercases the whole string with strings.ToLower before scanning the data part. Unicode case folding maps characters outside ASCII (for example U+212A KELVIN SIGN) onto bech32 charset characters, so a string that is invalid as given can fold into a short data part that later slicing assumes is at least checksum-length, panicking instead of returning an error.
defects.why_missed: The shipped suite only feeds ASCII vectors to Decode; nothing exercises non-ASCII input, and the fold-to-short-data-part path never runs, so the panic site stays untested. A test asserting only lowercase/uppercase ASCII equivalence stays green.
